text.p: AMSTERDAM, April 23( Reuter) - Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Cabinet is not reserving enough money in its 1998 budget to lower the budget deficit, says Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg. (p1)
- PM Wim Kok wants to increase tax on corporate executives capital gains from company share options as soon as possible. (p1)
- Bank insurer ING wants to buy a 50 pct stake in the World Trade Centre WTC in Amsterdam. (p1)
- Dutch insurance and pensions watchdog is to expand its staff from 115 to 160 over the next couple of years. (p1)
- German government is to file a claim against builder HBG and its subsidiary HBW for damages caused to the parliamentary buildings in 1993. (p3)
- KLM's U.S. partner Northwest Airlines reports stagnation of its Q1 results. (p3)
- Entertainment company PolyGram, 75-pct Philips owned, sees Q1 earnings drop to Dfl 122 million due to disappointing results of its film division. (p4)
- Royal Dutch/Shell studies possibilites of cooperation with Belgium's supermarket chain GB. (p4)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- PM Wim Kok sees the elections in France as an extra complication for the Dutch chairmanship of the European Union. (p1)
- Staff of financial daily Het Financieele Dagblad want to become joint owners of the paper. (p2)
- Reorganisation at insurance company Zurich Nederland will cost 126 jobs. (p2)
- Storage and transport concern Pakhoed books strong profit growth in first quarter. (p17)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Liberal party VVD furious about coalition partner D 66's refusal to support its plan to force unemployed to work for less than the minimum wage. (p3)
- Agricultural minister Jozias van Aartsen seeks to thoroughly restructure the pig breeding sector. (p9)
- Employers' association VNO-NCW and union FNV do not share DNB president Duisenberg's criticism of the 1998 budget. (p21)
- ABN Amro bank takes 80 percent interest in France's Banque Demachy Worms & Cie. (p23)
TROUW
- European central banks want to disclose exchange rates of their currencies against the Euro in May next year. (p1)
- Traffic minister Annemarie Jorritsma investigates possibility of a fourth mobile phone network. (p7) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Nearly half of the new products introduced on the Dutch market misfire -- TU Delft doctoral thesis. (p10)
- Graphical industry in the Netherlands is over its lows, according to branch organisation KVGO. (p10)
--Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
